258: And on that day Yitzchak crowned himself and he is the head of the Patriarchs. About that day it is written "In Tzion the sinners feared" (Isaiah 33:14). On that day Yitzchak bounded himself up, and everything was bound up, and Sarah wailed [diff. version: broke down], and the voice of the shofar was very strong. Happy is the lot of the one who passes through them and is saved from them. Rabbi Aba said: because of this we read the parashah of the Binding of Yitzchak on this day, because on this day Yitzchak bound himself up with the lower, and [so] connected/knotted himself with the One Above [diff. version: with Avraham]. When did he bound himself up?At the time when it is written "and he bound his son Yitzchak up" (Genesis 22:9).

Rabbi Eleazar said: On that day Yitzchak [gevurah/din] surrounded Avraham [gedulah/hesed] as it is written "And El-him tested Avraham" (Gen. 22:1). What is "nissah/tested"? As you say "and I will raise my banner/nissi to the peoples" (Isaiah 49:22). "And he called His name Ad-nai Nissi" (Exodus 17:15). What does this teach us? So that he would encompass the right and make himself complete. One [proof] is that it is written "And El-him tested Avraham". El-him, specifically, and this is "and the Fear of Isaac [Pachad Yitzchak]" (Genesis 31:42)

And when the messenger is as meritorious as he should be, that people merits with him. As all judgments retreat from them on account of him. All the more so with a priest. For with him, all of those in the upper realms and those in the lower realms are blessed. Rabbi Elazar said, "Because of this, before a priest or a Levite ascend to the service [of God], we inquire about him and find out his ways and his deeds. And if not, he does not ascend to the service. And likewise with the Sanhedrin to judge a case."

And if it is found that he is fit, we give him all the stringency of the Temple. But if not, he does not ascend to the service. This is [the meaning] of that which is written: And of Levi he said, "Let Your Thummim and Urim be with Your faithful one"(Deuteronomy 33:8). Why did (Aaron) merit the Urim and Thummim and to perform the service? You must say: Whom You tested, etc. Who said of his father and mother, I consider them not, etc. (Deuteronomy 33:8-9). And once he is found to be on these [proper] levels — then: They shall teach Your laws to Jacob, etc. they shall offer incense, etc., to calm the [divine] anger and to bring peace. And whole-offerings on Your altar (Deuteronomy 33:10). Since all is enriched, and blessing are found in all of the worlds, then: Bless, Lord, his substance, etc. (Deuteronomy 33:11).
